text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. Most APIs communicate through HTTP requests, which allow your application to send data to a server and receive a response. The data usually comes back in JSON format, a lightweight structure that is easy to read and parse. Before you can access an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key or token, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, always add proper error handling so your application can respond gracefully when something goes wrong, such as a network failure or an invalid request.
